 We're a couple of weeks into the NBA regular season, and the Miami Heat and Golden State Warriors are both looking for a win tonight. We've rounded up all the details on how to watch the Heat vs. Warriors, including live streaming options for those without cable.
 If you're hoping to tune in, we've got you covered. You can live stream the game on NBA TV via a live TV service like YouTube TV in the US, and through the NBA League Pass in the UK and most other international markets. You can access your usual streaming options from anywhere with a VPN, such as NordVPN .
 How to watch Heat vs. Warriors: quick links
 US: NBA TV
 YouTube TV (free trial) 
 Fubo (free trial) 
 UK & other countries: NBA League Pass (various) 
 Access accounts from anywhere: NordVPN (30-day money-back guarantee) 
 When: Thursday, November 5 at 7 p.m. PT / 10 p.m. ET / Friday at 3 a.m. GMT / 11 a.m. AWST
 What channel is the Heat vs. Warriors on?
 The Heat vs. Warriors game will be nationally broadcast on NBA TV in the US. The game is scheduled to tip off on Thursday at 10 p.m. ET, or 7 p.m. PT.

 How to watch the Heat vs. Warriors in the US
 Cord-cutters have several options when it comes to tuning into tonight's game. You can catch the network on a live TV streaming package. These month-to-month services work just like cable, without any long-term commitments.
 YouTube TV carries NBA TV and 100+ other popular channels in its Main plan. Subscriptions normally start at $83 a month, but a limited-time deal allows new users to get $15 a month off their first five months of service and a free trial.
 YouTube TV Main Plan
 YouTube TV's main plan carries over 100 channels, ranging from local networks to cable favorites.
 Check price at YouTube TV
 Fubo also offers NBA TV access, but you'll need to opt for the pricier Elite plan, which costs $99 a month and unlocks over 200 channels. First-time customers can get $30 off their first month after a free trial.
 Fubo Elite
 Fubo's base plan offers tons of classic channels, including local networks and traditional cable options, but the Elite tier unlocks 4K and even more sports-friendly options.
 Check price at Fubo
 How to watch the Heat vs. Warriors from anywhere
 For fans outside the US, games live stream on NBA League Pass in many international markets. Subscription prices vary from region to region. Some countries have other broadcast agreements for specific games. For example, Sky Sports shows a handful of NBA games each week in the UK (although not the Heat vs. Warriors match-up).
 That said, if you happen to be traveling through a region where you can't access your usual streaming services, it might be time to try a VPN (virtual private network). VPNs are easy-to-use tech tools that let people temporarily alter their virtual locations. This way, their favorite websites and apps function just like they would back home. Since the services we've recommended require country-specific payment methods, this option will work best for those who are just traveling away from home right now.
 Time and time again, NordVPN is one of the best VPNs we recommend. It's speedy, offers a nice selection of global servers, and has a 30-day money-back guarantee. You can learn more in our NordVPN review .
 NordVPN subscription
 NordVPN is top of the pile of the best VPN services. It offers excellent value, with a strong feature set and a low monthly price. A wide selection of international servers, high-end security, fast connections, and audited privacy protection have made the brand a household name in the world of VPNs for a reason.
 Check price at NordVPN
 How to use a VPN
 Sign up for a VPN if you don't already have one.
 Install it on the device you're planning to watch on.
 Turn it on and set it to the location of your streaming service.
 Navigate to your streaming service and create an account.
 Enjoy the game.
 Note: The use of VPNs is illegal in certain countries, and using VPNs to access region-locked streaming content might constitute a breach of the terms of use for certain services. Business Insider does not endorse or condone the illegal use of VPNs.
